title: seed-cluster-telemetry-ops-and-tf-patch-walkthrough
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for commissioning a small seed (control plane) cluster for private deployments with a focus on telemetry, safe TF module patches, and operator-friendly rotation steps. The goal is to document the exact commands, verification checks, and risk points we hit during the last 2 onprem pilot runs so teammates can reproduce and iterate.

Scope
- Initial network/DNS/KMS prep for seed control plane.
- Terraform module fixes we applied (and how) to avoid state drift.
- Lightweight telemetry stack recommendations (Prom, node-exporter, cp health metrics).
- Rotation procedures: KMS key rotation, CA cert roll, instance replacement.
- Canary/upgrade checks and rollback steps.

Quick summary of recommended stance
- Treat seed cluster as immutable for the first 72 hours after creation.
- Enable detailed telemetry retention for 7 days (hot) + 30 days (cold) for first-in-region seeds.
- Apply TF module patches as non-breaking follow-ups; prefer additive changes.

Prereqs (network + infra)
- VPC peering details: make sure peering set has route propagation to management CIDR (10.240.0.0/16).
- DNS: create A records in customer internal zone: cp-seed.{env}.{customer}.svc -> LB IP(s).
- KMS: create an envelope key with admin and operator principals defined; keep an export of key ID and rotation window.
- Inventory: record baremetal/node ids and BMC IPs in the session inventory spreadsheet.

Initial setup steps (high level)
1) Prep TF workspace
   - terraform workspace new seed-{customer}-{region} || use existing workspace
   - terraform init -upgrade
   - terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -out=tfplan.seed
2) Bootstrap infra (keep outputs small and copyable)
   - terraform apply "tfplan.seed"
   - copy outputs: seed_lb_ip, seed_vault_addr, seed_kms_key_id, seed_bootstrap_token
3) Bootstrap control plane services (example commands)
   - ssh operator@bootstrap-node 
     sudo /opt/redwood/bootstrap-controlplane --token ${seed_bootstrap_token} --kms ${seed_kms_key_id}
   - watch logs: journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -f
4) Verify KV cache and DB migrations
   - /opt/redwood/bin/rwctl db migrate status
   - rwctl cache inspect --prefix "seed:" | head -n 30

Terraform module notes (what we patched)
- Problem: module.aws_lb was recreating LB when backend health_check timeout changed (breaking).
  Fix applied: pin health_check to var.lb_health_check and added lifecycle ignore_changes = ["health_check.0.timeout"] for now.
  Why: customer's management plane had automated scripts altering timeout to 60s; we want TF to avoid recreating LB.
- Problem: kms_key resource lacked tags -> caused key rotation scripts to not find keys by tag.
  Fix: added tags = merge(var.common_tags, { "managed-by" = "redwood-cp" })
- Problem: state drift in module.node_pool when baremetal asset tags changed outside TF.
  Fix: added a node_pool.external_ids computed attribute and an import guide: `terraform import module.node_pool.redwood_node_pool.pool["N"] <asset-id>`
- Patch guidelines (team rules):
  - Minor fixes can go directly to infra branch with PR and 48h hold.
  - Any change that triggers resource replacement must have an explicit rollback plan spelled out in PR description.

Telemetry and alerting baseline
- Metrics to collect (minimal):
  - cp_request_latency_seconds{route,code}
  - cp_eviction_count_total
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio
  - controlplane_up (gauge per-instance)
  - prometheus_node_exporter:node_cpu_seconds_total (for system load spikes)

- Prometheus scrape config (notes): scrape_interval = 15s for cp endpoints, 30s for node-exporter.
- Alert rules (suggested):
  - cp_request_p95 > 250ms for 5m -> P2 latency alert
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m -> investigate caching layer
  - controlplane_up == 0 on more than 1 instance -> P1 outage runbook
- Dashboards: create a single seed cluster dashboard with the above metrics + a small traffic heatmap (token rate).

Rotation procedures (KMS / Node / Cert)
- KMS rotation (low-risk; can be automated):
  1) Create new key version in customer KMS (rotate window + alias to new key).
  2) Push config to controlplane: `rwctl config set encryption.kms_key_alias=alias/redwood-seed-new` (no restart)
  3) Run phased key rewrap: `rwctl crypto rewrap --from-key ${old} --to-key ${new} --batch-size 1000` and monitor rewrap progress.
  4) When rewrap at 100% and background jobs are idle, retire old key after 48h.
  Verification: `rwctl crypto status --key ${new}` shows 100% rewrapped keys.

- CA cert rotation (medium-risk; requires rolling restart):
  1) Generate new CA and intermediate certs in KMS-backed vault.
  2) Upload to /etc/redwood/pki/new/ and validate `openssl x509 -in new.pem -noout -text` matches expected SANs.
  3) Restart first controlplane instance with `systemctl restart redwood-controlplane` and watch connectivity for 10m.
  4) If stable, roll to remaining instances one-by-one with a 2m pause to let caches warm.
  5) If any instance fails health checks for >5m, run immediate rollback on that node: `systemctl start redwood-controlplane --force` and restore old cert symlink.

- Instance/node rotation (higher-risk; reusable playbook):
  - Drain: `rwctl node drain <node-id> --timeout 600` (failsafe: `--force`)
  - Disable from loadbalancer: `aws elb deregister-instances --instance-id <id>` or equivalent BMC API call.
  - Replace: provision new baremetal or new vm using module.node_pool (terraform apply).
  - Import: `terraform import module.node_pool.redwood_node_pool.pool["<name>"] <asset-id>` then run `terraform plan` to reconcile tags.
  - Re-enable LB and uncordon: `rwctl node uncordon <node-id>` and health-check for 10m.

Upgrade plan (APIs + runtime)
- Version pinning: set `controlplane.version = "vX.Y.Z"` in var files. Always increment minor for non-breaking, major for DB migrations.
- Canary rollout strategy:
  1) Create canary group: select 1 instance in each AZ (or 1 AZ if single-region).
  2) Apply update to canary only via `terraform apply -target=module.node_pool.redwood_node_pool.pool["canary"]` + `rwctl deploy start --group canary`
  3) Smoke tests: run `./scripts/smoke-smith.sh --seed ${seed_lb_ip}` which runs token round-trip, KV get/set, and a small load test (50 qps for 60s).
  4) If metrics stable and no errors, expand to 25% -> 50% -> 100% by repeating targetted deploys.

Rollback checklist (if canary fails)
- Immediate: divert traffic by updating route policy to fallback model (rwctl router set-route --policy fallback) and scale down canary group.
- Recreate previous TF plan: `terraform apply -var controlplane.version=vPrevious -auto-approve` on the workspace.
- If DB migration failed: `rwctl db migrate rollback --to-version vPrevious` (only safe if migration is reversible; avoid irreversible schema changes without gating).

Post-change verification (automated)
- run `./scripts/check-seed-health.sh ${seed_lb_ip}` (this runs API health, ping, cache checks, prom queries)
- Ensure alerts are firing/clearing in Alertmanager: check silence status and clear stale silences for the seed cluster.

Common failure modes we hit & mitigations
- LB recreation due to health-check param drift -> mitigation: ignore_changes in TF and manual reconciler patch.
- Cold-cache storm after rotation leading to 5–10x token generation latency -> mitigation: pre-warm caches with synthetic requests using rwctl prewarm --prefix "." --rate 200/s for 5m.
- BMC flakiness on baremetal -> mitigation: prefer VM artifact for initial commissioning, then gradually move to baremetal after 48h of stable telemetry.

Runbook commands (copyable)
- Terraform init + plan: `export TF_VAR_customer="acme"; terraform workspace select seed-acme-usw2 || terraform workspace new seed-acme-usw2; terraform init; terraform plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars -out tfplan.seed`
- Apply with auto-approve for emergency rollback only: `terraform apply -auto-approve tfplan.seed`
- Health check smoke: `curl -sS https://${seed_lb_ip}/health | jq` (expect JSON {"ok":true})

Telemetry troubleshooting checklist
- Check prometheus target scrape status: visit /targets on prometheus web UI.
- If controlplane_up shows 0 for a single instance -> check systemd logs: `journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -n 200`
- If kv_cache_hit_ratio drops suddenly -> run `rwctl cache snapshot --size 1000` and inspect hit/miss distribution.

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] Decide canonical scrape interval for seed clusters (15s vs 30s). 15s provides better fidelity but increases storage/cost.
- [ ] Finalize terraform module contract for node external_ids so imports are predictable.
- [ ] Add automated prewarm job in our deploy pipeline for any node replacement.
- [ ] Document vendor-specific BMC quirks per customer in a small table (IPMI timeout, BIOS quirks).

Notes-to-self (less formal)
- When we last rotated CA, we missed one HA proxy config that referenced the old cert path; add validation to smoke script to check HA proxy cert file.
- Consider adding an operator CLI command `rwctl seed-checklist generate --short` that prints the minimal verification steps for on-call.

Appendix: useful script snippets
- prewarm.sh (one-liner): `seq 1 1000 | xargs -P10 -I{} curl -sS -X POST https://${seed_lb_ip}/generate -d '{"prompt":"warmup"}' >/dev/null`
- check-seed-health.sh snippet: `curl -sS https://${seed_lb_ip}/metrics | grep cp_request_latency_seconds | tail -n1`

If anything in here is unclear, ping me (Maya) or comment on the linked PR. This doc is intentionally operational and terse — meant to be a working artifact that we update after each seed run.
